definition: Impede means to slow or hinder the progress of something without stopping it altogether.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word impede. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know impede should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Fog impeded the search all night without ever ending it; the boats simply moved at a crawl between calls.
Delay is milder than impede — the shipment still arrives whole, just later than the paper promised; nothing about the going itself was made heavier.
Paralyze goes further than impede — impeded traffic still crawls forward; paralyzed traffic stands dead where it is.

To bog down is the mud picture of impeding: progress that labors on under the weight, wheels spinning and gaining a little less each hour. Impede is the wider, cooler verb — any drag at all, fog or paperwork or friction — the word an engineer's report uses where a complaint says bogged down.

Obstruct means to put a thing in the path — a fallen tree, a parked truck, a filed objection. Impede needs no obstacle at all: fog or friction can impede a voyage that nothing actually blocks. Obstruct names the thing in the way; impede measures the drag.
